text:
maya: quick question — for the air-gapped/private deploys, do we have a documented flow for sending audit logs out to the customer's SIEM without opening full egress?
ben: not fully documented. current plan was a write-only collector that pulls from local audit stream and pushes to a customer-configured forwarder over a single allowed port.
ravi: correct. we only allow outbound to fixed IPs via fw rules, TLS mutual auth, and cert pinned to HSM-backed key.
sophia: from SRE side we worry about proof the agent is truly write-only (no sockets listening for inbound). any suggestions?
maya: two ideas: kernel-level egress-only iptables rules + run the collector in an unprivileged container with no hostNetwork. also limit capabilities CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE etc.
ben: quick sketch of iptables egress rule we tested:
```bash
# allow outbound to collector IP, drop all other outbound
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 10.20.30.40/32 -p tcp --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 1:65535 -j DROP
```
maya: also recommend a k8s NetworkPolicy that only allows egress to the collector service and blocks pod-to-pod egress for that namespace.
ben: example NP we used for the collector namespace: 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-only-to-collector
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-collector
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.20.30.40/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
ravi: big question on keying — customers ask HSM-backed KMS integration where the collector signs the TLS client cert with their key. we can't store customer CA on control plane. any ops constraints?
maya: we should support a customer-provided KMS plugin endpoint in the private deployment: collector gets a signing token that only calls KMS to sign CSR, never exports private key. HSM does the signing. we need local attestation so customer can verify certificate origin.
sophia: how does this impact upgrades and rotation? if KMS revokes a key during rollout, collectors must fail closed (stop sending) and signal via ops channel. need graceful fallback or manual override.
ben: propose rollout steps: 1) enable collector in dry-run (local logs only) 2) smoke test outbound to staging forwarder 3) enable egress firewall + pin IPs 4) enable KMS signing + rotation window 5) enable production forwarder.
maya: add automated vuln triage step: collector container should run with read-only filesystem, signed image, SBOM attached to release, and automated CVE scan before marking deployable.
audit-bot: vuln scan result: audit-collector:1.2.3 — 0 critical, 2 high (libcrypto outdated).
ravi: ok patch libcrypto in next image. timeline?
sophia: can we hotfix only collector images for customers on private? we should support patch-only channel.
ben: yes, Dedicated/Private supports patch-only builds — coordinate with release-engineering.
maya: last point on RBAC: create a dedicated k8s service account with only permissions to read the audit log path and write to the collector. no cluster-admin. document the exact RBAC role in the deploy guide.
sophia: +1. also add incident playbook snippet: if collector stops sending, run `kubectl logs -n audit-collector` and `tcpdump -i eth0 port 443` from a bastion with approved access. escalate to sec-oncall if evidence of outbound to unknown IPs.
ravi: I'll draft the deploy guide and RBAC YAML, push to the private-deploy repo, and share PR. @maya can you own the KMS/HSM integration spec?
maya: yep, will draft and include attestation pattern and rotation policy.
ben: thanks — once PR is up i'll run through the egress tests with SRE and report back. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deployment trigger registered by ben for audit-collector:1.2.4-staging
